stemMarkdown: Let $f(x) = x^2 + 1$ and $g(x) = \sqrt{x}$. What is the value of $(f \circ g)(9)$?
solutionMarkdown:
$(f \circ g)(9) = f(g(9))$. First, find $g(9)$: $$
g(x) = \sqrt{x} 
\Rightarrow g(9) = \sqrt{9} = 3
$$ Now apply $f$ to the value obtained from $g$: $$
f(x) = x^2 + 1 
\Rightarrow f(g(9)) = f(3) = 3^2 + 1 = 9 + 1 = 10.
$$ Hence, $(f \circ g)(9) = 10.$
altSolutionMarkdown: Since $g(x)$ takes the square root and $f(x)$ then squares it back up while adding 1, substitute 9 into $g$, yielding 3. Then input 3 in $f$ to get $3^2 + 1 = 10$. This skips manual function composition notation.
